tax.text: Barr voted for the 2025 tax law, which he described as a historic tax cut.
tax.quote: Andy has always fought for tax cuts. In 2025, he voted for the largest tax cut in American history, the Big Beautiful Bill.

wages.text: Barr voted against the Raise the Wage Act, which would have increased the federal minimum wage.
wages.quote: Jul 18, 2019, 12:01 PM | 116th Congress, 1st Session Vote Question: On Passage Raise the Wage Act

housing.text: Barr voted for legislation to expand housing supply and cut red tape to accelerate homebuilding.
housing.quote: This bipartisan bill tackles the housing shortage by cutting red tape, empowering community lenders, and unlocking private investment.

schools.text: Barr cosponsored legislation to fund scholarships for students attending public, independent, or religious schools.
schools.quote: This legislation will boost resources to expand school choice without raising taxes on a single Kentuckian.

safety.text: Barr says he supports police and has voted to increase federal law enforcement funding.
safety.quote: Andy Barr strongly supports police and will work with them to help keep Kentucky safe.

sentencing.text: Barr voted for the First Step Act, a criminal justice reform law that included changes to sentencing and prison programs.
sentencing.quote: Dec 20, 2018, 01:58 PM | 115th Congress, 2nd Session Vote Question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in the Senate Amendment to House Amendment First Step Act of 2018

immigration.text: Barr says he supports deporting undocumented people with criminal convictions and strengthening border security.
immigration.quote: Andy Barr believes we must deport all criminal illegals and secure the border.

guns.text: Barr says he opposes gun control bills and supports protecting gun owners’ Second Amendment rights.
guns.quote: Andy has consistently opposed gun control bills put forward to strip gun owners of their firearms without due process.

abortion.text: Barr said he would continue supporting federal policies that restrict abortion, including the Hyde Amendment.
abortion.quote: At the federal level, I will continue to support pro-life policies in Congress such as the Hyde Amendment, to prohibit taxpayer funding of abortions

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Barr supports restricting girls’ sports participation and school funding based on sex rather than gender identity.
gender.quote: He’s leading the Defend Girls’ Athletics Act that cuts off federal funding to any school or university that refuses to uphold the ban on biological men in girls’ sports.

cannabis.text: Barr voted against the MORE Act, which would have removed marijuana from the federal controlled-substances list and regulated it.
cannabis.quote: Dec 04, 2020, 01:08 PM | 116th Congress, 2nd Session Vote Question: On Passage MORE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

health.text: Barr backed replacing the Affordable Care Act with reforms he described as market based and designed to encourage competition.
health.quote: I promised the people of the Sixth District that I would vote to repeal this broken law and replace it with reforms that will actually lower costs and expand access to care through patient-centered, market-based reforms.

energy.text: Barr says his energy plan would expand coal production, create jobs, and lower energy costs.
energy.quote: Andy has a plan to bring back clean, beautiful coal, to create jobs, lower energy costs, and attract industries of the future to Kentucky.

voting.text: Barr backed legislation requiring voter ID and proof of citizenship for federal elections and supported tighter voter-roll rules.
voting.quote: The SAVE America Act addresses these gaps directly by requiring photo ID to cast a ballot, mandating documentary proof of U.S. citizenship for federal voter registration, requiring regular voter roll maintenance, and providing clear procedures to protect eligible voters from administrative discrepancies.

tax.text: He said closing tax loopholes could help fund health care.
tax.quote: WE CLOSE LOOPHOLES, BRING MORE MONEY MOOT SYSTEM, WE CAN AFFORD TO HAVE HEALTHCARE FOR THE PEOPLE OF KENTUCKY.

housing.text: Booker proposes building more affordable housing and expanding tenant protections.
housing.quote: We will build more affordable housing, implement federal rent stabilization, strengthen tenant protections like just-cause eviction and the right to counsel, and make major investments to end homelessness.

safety.text: Booker said public safety budgets should address poverty and that arrests alone cannot make society safer.
safety.quote: That means we should make sure our budgets address poverty and the social determinants of health, instead of continuing to balloon budgets with a growing, militarized law enforcement.

immigration.text: He proposed abolishing ICE and replacing it with an enforcement system without mass detention or blanket deportation.
immigration.quote: Abolish ICE by ending funding for the agency and dismantling it entirely

guns.text: Booker said he had fought for gun safety reform as a state legislator.
guns.quote: As a legislator, I fought for common sense gun safety reform, lower prescription drug prices, expanded voting rights, stronger labor unions, and for racial justice.

abortion.text: Booker said he would support legislation to codify Roe v. Wade.
abortion.quote: Also on my docket are expanding medicare, codifying Roe v Wade, and legalizing marijuana.

cannabis.text: Booker said legalizing marijuana was among the legislation he would pursue in Washington.
cannabis.quote: Also on my docket are expanding medicare, codifying Roe v Wade, and legalizing marijuana.

health.text: Booker supports Medicare for All to provide health care to everyone.
health.quote: We should ensure that everyone has high-quality health care with Medicare for All.

energy.text: Booker called for clean energy investment and a transition toward new industries, including zero-emission technologies.
energy.quote: To take this on, we must start by making the vital investments in our infrastructure to clean our land and foster a clean energy economy.

voting.text: He supports strengthening the Voting Rights Act and expanding early and mail voting.
voting.quote: I support restoring and strengthening the Voting Rights Act, significantly expanding early and mail voting

wages.text: He identifies as a union member and says workers should receive quality pay and have protection when raising grievances.
wages.quote: All American workers disserve to work in safe environments, with excellent benefits and quality pay. Additionally, those workers must have a means to address grievances without fear of retaliation or retribution.

abortion.text: He says reproductive care is health care and supports each person's control over their own body, including during pregnancy.
abortion.quote: Reproductive Care is Health Care and no American citizen should be deprived of it.

energy.text: He proposes environmental protections and legislation to prevent companies from using carbon credits to continue polluting.
energy.quote: As a Senator of Kentucky, I would push for legislation to eliminate the ability of companies to purchase Carbon Credits, which simply allow facilities to continue polluting as they pay third-parties to develop “green” projects.
